page: Microsoft Azure M64 is a memory-optimized virtual machine engineered for enterprise applications demanding massive physical memory allocations and dedicated computing resources. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, the platform utilizes an Intel Xeon 8280M processor built on x86_64 architecture running at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The hardware configuration delivers 64 vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores via two threads per core, backed by 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a shared 38 MB L3 cache. Vector extensions include AVX and AVX-512F alongside cryptographic AES instructions. System memory totals 1024 GB, yielding an expansive 16 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is addressed via 7697 GB of integrated local solid-state drive capacity, while hardware accelerators are absent with zero GPUs provisioned.

Benchmark assessments underscore a system heavily biased toward memory throughput and multi-threaded scaling rather than single-threaded execution speed. Single-core evaluations reflect architectural constraints of the Cascade Lake platform, scoring in the lower percentiles for Geekbench (917.0), single-thread stress-ng (1038.59), and gzip compression (17.35 GB/sec). Conversely, parallelized and memory-subsystem tests reveal solid execution capabilities. Multi-core stress-ng reached 43764.35, while PassMark database operations and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression delivered stable mid-tier results. Crucially, memory bandwidth performance is robust under sustained transfer conditions, achieving 216.37 GB/sec in large-block uncached read operations alongside 2438.45 GB/sec in cached small-block reads.

From a cost efficiency and architectural perspective, the M64 trades per-core execution latency for high physical memory density and bundled local storage capacity. Deploying this server for single-threaded processing, text generation, or standard web serving represents an inefficient use of resources due to moderate CPU clock limits. Instead, the balance of 1024 GB RAM, fast memory interconnect bandwidth, and 40.55 million Redis SET operations per second makes it an effective deployment target for large in-memory databases, SAP HANA, memory-resident analytics, distributed cache nodes, and enterprise relational database engines requiring large buffer pools.
description: Microsoft Azure M64 is a memory-optimized enterprise cloud server built for data-intensive workloads requiring extensive memory footprints. Powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8280M processors running at 2.7 GHz on Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance provides 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, supporting AVX-512 extensions. Memory capacity is substantial at 1024 GB, establishing a 16 GB per-core ratio, alongside 7697 GB of bundled local SSD storage. Benchmark results show modest single-core throughput, with Geekbench single-core and compression tests placing in lower percentiles. However, the system delivers strong uncached large-block read memory bandwidth of 216.37 GB/sec and consistent multi-threaded compute capability across PassMark and stress-ng evaluations. With 40.55 million Redis SET operations per second, the architecture is cost-efficient for heavy memory-bound deployments, trading per-core clock speed for immense density. Azure M64 is best suited for large in-memory databases such as SAP HANA, massive key-value stores, real-time analytics engines, and enterprise data processing.
